//: `include` is explicit and MUST stay limited to src/.
There is no `rootDir`, so tsc infers one from the common ancestor of every input file.
While that was only ever src/, the output was dist/<domain>/... — which is what the entity
globs in src/database/data-source.ts ('dist/*/entity/*.entity.js') are written against.
Adding a single .ts file anywhere outside src/ (a build script, a codegen helper) moves that
inferred root up to the repo root, and every emitted path gains a `src/` segment. Nothing
fails to compile — the app starts, /api/health returns 200, migrations run — but the entity
glob silently matches zero files and every request that touches an entity dies with
EntityMetadataNotFoundError. Adding scripts/ did exactly that.
Keep dev-only tooling out of the build. scripts/ runs through `ts-node -T`, which does not
need to be in the project's include set.
